title: Embedded Memory, Startup & the Build
relevance: Tests whether candidates understand bare-metal program startup, memory sections, and the linker/build path that firmware interviews and OAs routinely probe.

phases.goal: Establish how a microcontroller's on-chip memory is physically divided and what each region holds.

must_hit.point: Flash/ROM is non-volatile: it retains data when power is lost and houses compiled code, .rodata, and initial templates for initialized variables.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says Flash keeps contents across power loss and stores code plus read-only/init templates.

must_hit.point: RAM is volatile: it loses contents on power loss and holds .data, .bss, the call stack, and the heap.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts RAM volatility with Flash and lists live globals, stack, and heap.

must_hit.point: Peripherals such as timers or serial ports are mapped into memory addresses; writing those addresses configures the hardware.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes MMIO: hardware registers appear as addresses you read/write.

probes: On a bare-metal MCU, what lives in Flash versus RAM, and what happens to each on power loss?

hints.1: Think about which memory survives a power cut and which is the live workspace.
hints.2: Name the common sections: code/.rodata in Flash; .data, .bss, stack, heap in RAM.
hints.3: Flash/ROM is non-volatile (code, .rodata, init templates); RAM is volatile (.data, .bss, stack, heap); peripherals are memory-mapped.

phases.goal: Explain how reset, crt0, and the linker script initialize static storage and place sections before main.

must_hit.point: On reset the CPU reads a hardcoded address for the initial stack pointer and Reset Handler (often crt0), which prepares the environment before main.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes vector-table reset entry and that main is not the first code run.

must_hit.point: crt0 copies initialized .data from Flash into RAM and zeroes .bss; only then does it call main(), fulfilling static-storage initialization.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names the Flash→RAM copy for .data and the zeroing of .bss before main.

must_hit.point: Because RAM is volatile, .data has an LMA in Flash and a VMA in RAM; crt0 copies from LMA to VMA.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate defines LMA as load/storage address and VMA as execution address, with .data spanning both.

must_hit.point: The linker script's MEMORY and SECTIONS commands map input sections to physical regions and export boundary symbols (e.g. _sdata) that startup uses as copy bookmarks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says the linker places sections and exports symbols startup walks to copy/zero memory.

must_hit.point: The vector table is an array of function pointers at a fixed address; the linker places it at the start of FLASH, commonly via .isr_vector.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate ties earliest entries (stack pointer, Reset Handler) to a linker-forced vector section at Flash start.

probes: What is the difference between VMA and LMA for the .data section, and who uses the linker symbols between them?

hints.1: Ask where initialized globals live at rest versus where the CPU uses them at run time.
hints.2: Separate load address (Flash) from execution address (RAM), then name the copy loop in the Reset Handler.
hints.3: VMA is where code/data is expected when executing; LMA is permanent storage. For .data, LMA is Flash, VMA is RAM; crt0 copies using linker symbols like _sdata/_edata/_sidata.

phases.goal: Show how declaration and allocation choices trade Flash vs RAM, and how library I/O can blow the memory budget.

must_hit.point: const goes in Flash (.rodata); initialized globals consume both Flash and RAM (.data); zero-initialized globals use only RAM (.bss).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate maps const / initialized / zero-init to .rodata / both Flash+RAM / .bss-only.

must_hit.point: On bare metal, const lookup tables or string literals save RAM by keeping data exclusively in Flash.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate explicitly says const is a RAM-saving placement choice, not only type safety.

must_hit.point: Without retargeting, linking printf can pull massive generic I/O handlers that exhaust Flash/RAM; .map files audit per-function cost.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate warns about printf size and mentions auditing with a map file or implementing a small _write path.

probes: Why mark a large lookup table const on a microcontroller, and what goes wrong if you link printf without retargeting?

hints.1: Compare where the linker puts const versus a non-const global with an initializer.
hints.2: Initialized globals pay twice (Flash template + RAM live copy); const pays once in Flash.
hints.3: const → .rodata in Flash only; initialized globals → Flash+RAM; bare printf without _write/UART retarget can bloat the image—check the .map.

phases.goal: Connect the toolchain, retargeting, and failure modes (soft reset, overflow, stack collision) to real bare-metal builds.

must_hit.point: Cross-compilation targets a different ISA (e.g. arm-none-eabi-gcc with -mcpu); -T supplies the linker script; objcopy extracts .bin/.hex for flashing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names host≠target, the prefixed toolchain, linker script flag, and raw image via objcopy.

must_hit.point: newlib/newlib-nano need retargeting—implement a low-level hook such as _write that sends characters to a UART—so printf works without an OS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes implementing _write (or equivalent) to route stdio to hardware UART.

must_hit.point: Stack typically grows downward from high RAM while .data/.bss sit low; deep recursion or huge locals can silently overwrite globals (stack overflow).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes opposing growth directions and silent corruption of globals on collision.

must_hit.point: A soft reset that jumps to main without re-running crt0 leaves .data/.bss stale; the same risk appears with bad bootloader handoff or waking from deep sleep that powered down RAM.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate refuses to equate soft reset with full startup and names re-init after sleep/bootloader.

probes: If a soft reset jumps straight to main, what happens to your globals—and how do you prevent stack/.bss collision on a small MCU?

hints.1: Soft reset is not the same as power-on unless the Reset Handler runs again.
hints.2: Trace: skip crt0 → no .data copy / .bss zero; separately, stack descending into globals.
hints.3: Jumping to main without crt0 keeps stale .data/.bss; prefer static allocation and bounded stacks so requirements are compile-time proven.

tradeoffs.topic: const (.rodata in Flash) vs initialized globals (.data in Flash and RAM)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: const keeps data only in Flash and saves RAM; initialized non-const globals store a Flash template and a live RAM copy, so they consume both.

tradeoffs.topic: Static allocation vs heap and deep stacks
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prefer static allocation so Flash/RAM needs are known at link/compile time; heap growing up from .bss and deep/downward stacks invite runtime OOM and silent stack–global collisions.

tradeoffs.topic: Retargeted printf (_write to UART) vs linking printf without retargeting
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Retargeting routes characters through a small UART hook; without it, generic I/O handlers can exhaust the MCU memory budget—audit with a .map file.

gotchas.trap: Assuming a software soft reset automatically reinitializes globals.
gotchas.correction: If the soft reset jumps to main without re-running crt0, .data and .bss keep stale values.

gotchas.trap: Custom bootloader handoff or deep-sleep wake that skips the Flash→RAM copy / .bss zero.
gotchas.correction: Re-execute the initialization path after handoff or when RAM was powered down.

gotchas.trap: Code or data growing past MEMORY LENGTH in the linker script.
gotchas.correction: The link fails with a region overflowed error; shrink usage or fix LENGTH/layout.

gotchas.trap: Huge locals or deep recursion on a bare-metal stack.
gotchas.correction: The downward-growing stack can overwrite .data/.bss; prefer static allocation and bounded stack depth.

gotchas.trap: Calling printf on bare metal without retargeting the C library.
gotchas.correction: Implement _write (or equivalent) to a UART, or avoid heavy stdio; otherwise link size can explode.
